# `bench` standard library

The `bench` module provides monotonic-clock microbenchmarking with automatic warmup iterations, per-iteration latency percentiles (`min`, `p50`, `p95`, `p99`, `max`), arena allocation tracking (`mem::current_provenance!`), and throughput reporting.

```{.dva .run}
#use bench
#use io

r = bench::measure(100, i => i * i + 1)
s = bench::measure_stats(50, i => (i * 17 + 3) % 97)
io::out $ (r.iters, s.iters, s.min_ns !> s.p95_ns, s.p95_ns !> s.max_ns)
```

## Types and Function catalog

| Symbol / Function | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `bench::BenchResult` | Record `(iters: Int, total_ns: Int, avg_ns: Float, ops_per_sec: Float)` | Aggregate throughput timing result |
| `bench::StatsResult` | Record `(iters, total_ns, avg_ns, min_ns, p50_ns, p95_ns, p99_ns, max_ns, ops_per_sec, alloc_bytes, alloc_chunks)` | Latency distribution and arena allocation result |
| `bench::start!` | `() => Int` | Captures a monotonic starting timestamp in nanoseconds |
| `bench::elapsed_ns(t0)` | `Int => Int` | Returns nanoseconds elapsed since `t0` (from `bench::start!`) |
| `bench::elapsed_ms(t0)` | `Int => Float` | Returns milliseconds elapsed since `t0` |
| `bench::measure(iters, fn)` | `Int, (Int => Int) => BenchResult` | Runs 10% warmup iterations then times `iters` invocations of `fn(i)` |
| `bench::format(name, res)` | `String, BenchResult => String` | Formats `BenchResult` into a single throughput line |
| `bench::run(name, iters, fn)` | `String, Int, (Int => Int) => BenchResult` | Measures `fn` and prints the formatted line to stdout |
| `bench::measure_stats(iters, fn)` | `Int, (Int => Int) => StatsResult` | Records per-iteration sorted latencies (`min`..`max`) and active arena byte/chunk allocations |
| `bench::format_stats(name, res)` | `String, StatsResult => String` | Formats `StatsResult` with `min`/`p50`/`p95`/`p99`/`max` and `alloc=` summary |
| `bench::run_stats(name, iters, fn)` | `String, Int, (Int => Int) => StatsResult` | Measures `fn` with stats and prints the formatted summary to stdout |
